_about: The image side by side (plan 7.6b): places that speak of humankind made in the image and likeness of God, and of an image borne or renewed, in the passages' own words, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi. Psalms & elsewhere: any other Old Testament book.

rows.title: Made in His own image

Genesis: Let Us make man in Our image
So God created man in His own image
for in His own image God has made mankind
The letters: conformed to the image of His Son
are being transformed into His image
which is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator

rows.alike: Each speaks of people and an image: Genesis says "God created man in His own image", and the letters speak of being "conformed to the image of His Son", "transformed into His image" and "renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator".
rows.different: Genesis 1:26 has God say "Let Us make man in Our image", and Genesis 9:6 gives "for in His own image God has made mankind" as the reason in its sentence on bloodshed; the letters say "conformed to the image of His Son" (Romans 8:29), "transformed into His image" (2 Corinthians 3:18) and "renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator" (Colossians 3:10).

rows.title: In His own likeness

Genesis: He made him in His own likeness
he had a son in his own likeness, after his own image
The letters: we have borne the likeness of the earthly man
so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man
men, who have been made in God's likeness

rows.alike: Genesis 1:26 says "after Our likeness", Genesis 5:1 "He made him in His own likeness" and James "men, who have been made in God's likeness"; Genesis 5:3 and 1 Corinthians 15:49 also use "likeness", of a man: "in his own likeness", "the likeness of the earthly man".
rows.different: Genesis 5:3 says Adam "had a son in his own likeness, after his own image"; 1 Corinthians 15:49 sets "the likeness of the earthly man", which "we have borne", beside "the likeness of the heavenly man", which "shall we bear". James says it of the people the tongue curses.

rows.title: The image of God

Genesis: in the image of God He created him
The letters: he is the image and glory of God
the glory of Christ, who is the image of God
The Son is the image of the invisible God
The Son is the radiance of God's glory and the exact representation of His nature

rows.alike: The words "the image of God" stand in Genesis 1:27 and 2 Corinthians 4:4; 1 Corinthians 11:7 has "the image and glory of God" and Colossians 1:15 has "the image of the invisible God".
rows.different: Genesis says of man that God created him "in the image of God", and goes on "male and female He created them"; 1 Corinthians 11:7 says of "A man" that "he is the image and glory of God", and goes on "but the woman is the glory of man"; 2 Corinthians 4:4 says it of Christ and Colossians 1:15 of "The Son". Hebrews 1:3 has no word "image" but opens the same way, "The Son is the", with "the radiance of God's glory and the exact representation of His nature".

rows.title: The likeness of a man

The Prophets: His form was marred beyond human likeness
a figure like that of a man
one with the likeness of a man touched my lips
the one with the likeness of a man touched me
He fashions it in the likeness of man
Psalms & elsewhere: in the likeness of a male or female
The letters: sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man

rows.alike: Each speaks of a likeness to man: "beyond human likeness", "a figure like that of a man", "the likeness of a man", "in the likeness of sinful man", "in human likeness".
rows.different: Isaiah 52:14 says "His form was marred beyond human likeness"; Ezekiel sees on the throne "a figure like that of a man", and Daniel tells of "one with the likeness of a man" who "touched my lips"; Romans says God sent "His own Son in the likeness of sinful man" and Philippians says "being made in human likeness". Isaiah 44:13 and Deuteronomy 4:16 use the words of a figure made by hand: the woodworker "fashions it in the likeness of man", and Deuteronomy forbids an idol "in the likeness of a male or female".

rows.title: What is man?

Psalms & elsewhere: What is man that You should exalt him, that You should set Your heart upon him
what is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?
O LORD, what is man, that You regard him, the son of man that You think of him?
The letters: But somewhere it is testified in these words
What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?

rows.alike: All four put the question "what is man" to God, and Psalm 8, Psalm 144 and Hebrews 2 pair it with "the son of man". Hebrews 2:6 has the words of Psalm 8:4.
rows.different: Psalm 8 goes on "that You are mindful of him", Psalm 144 "that You regard him", and Job "that You should exalt him". Hebrews introduces the words with "But somewhere it is testified in these words".

rows.title: A little lower than the angels, crowned with glory and honor

Psalms & elsewhere: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor
The letters: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor
But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death

rows.alike: Psalm 8:5 and Hebrews 2:7 have the same words: "You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor".
rows.different: Hebrews 2:9 says "we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor", and adds "because He suffered death".

rows.title: Everything under his feet

Psalms & elsewhere: You have placed everything under his feet
The letters: God has put everything under His feet
this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him
And God put everything under His feet and made Him head over everything for the church
and placed everything under his feet
Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him
put all His enemies under His feet

rows.alike: Each says everything is put under someone's feet: "You have placed everything under his feet", "God has put everything under His feet", "God put everything under His feet", "placed everything under his feet"; 1 Corinthians 15:25 says "put all His enemies under His feet".
rows.different: Psalm 8 speaks to God, "You have placed"; 1 Corinthians and Ephesians say "God has put" and "God put". Ephesians adds "made Him head over everything for the church", 1 Corinthians adds "this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him", and Hebrews adds "Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him". In 1 Corinthians 15:25 it is "all His enemies" put under His feet, "until" He has done so.

rows.title: By man his blood will be shed

Genesis: I will demand an accounting from anyone who takes the life of his fellow man
Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood will be shed; for in His own image God has made mankind
Psalms & elsewhere: no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it

rows.alike: Both speak of the blood of the one who sheds blood: "by man his blood will be shed", "except by the blood of the one who shed it".
rows.different: Genesis 9:6 gives as its reason "for in His own image God has made mankind"; Numbers 35:33 speaks of the land: "bloodshed pollutes the land".

rows.title: Blessing and cursing from the same mouth

Psalms & elsewhere: they delight in lies; with their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse
The letters: With the tongue we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse men, who have been made in God's likeness
Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, this should not be

rows.alike: Both set blessing and cursing in one mouth: "with their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse", "Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing".
rows.different: Psalm 62 speaks of others, who "delight in lies" and "inwardly" curse; James says "we", blessing "our Lord and Father" and cursing "men, who have been made in God's likeness", and adds "this should not be".

rows.title: No one has ever seen God

Psalms & elsewhere: You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live
Gospels & Acts: No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father's side, has made Him known
Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father
The letters: the image of the invisible God
the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God
he persevered because he saw Him who is invisible
No one has ever seen God; but if we love one another, God remains in us
No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him

rows.alike: John 1:18 and 1 John 4:12 have the same words, "No one has ever seen God", and 1 Timothy 6:16 has "No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him"; Exodus 33:20 has "no one can see Me and live", and Colossians and 1 Timothy call God "invisible".
rows.different: John 1:18 adds that the Son "has made Him known", and in John 14:9 Jesus says "Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father"; Colossians calls the Son "the image of the invisible God"; 1 John adds "if we love one another, God remains in us"; Hebrews says of Moses "he saw Him who is invisible".

rows.title: The firstborn

Psalms & elsewhere: I will indeed appoint him as My firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth
The letters: He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers
The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation
He is the beginning and firstborn from among the dead
when God brings His firstborn into the world
Revelation: Revelation 1:5
the firstborn from the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth

rows.alike: Romans 8:29 and Colossians 1:15 both set "firstborn" beside "image": "the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn", "the image of the invisible God, the firstborn". Colossians 1:18 and Revelation 1:5 both have "firstborn from" the dead, and Psalm 89:27 and Revelation 1:5 both join firstborn to "the kings of the earth".
rows.different: In Psalm 89 God speaks: "I will indeed appoint him as My firstborn". The places complete "firstborn" differently: "over all creation", "from among the dead", "among many brothers", "the highest of the kings of the earth"; Revelation adds "the ruler of the kings of the earth".

rows.title: A veil over his face

Psalms & elsewhere: his face had become radiant from speaking with the LORD
he put a veil over his face
he would remove the veil until he came out
Moses would put the veil back over his face
The letters: the Israelites could not gaze at the face of Moses because of its fleeting glory
We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away
whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away
And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory

rows.alike: Exodus and 2 Corinthians both tell of Moses' face and the veil: "he put a veil over his face", "who would put a veil over his face"; Exodus has "he would remove the veil" and, in 34:35, "Moses would put the veil back over his face", and 2 Corinthians "the veil is taken away" when anyone "turns to the Lord".
rows.different: Exodus says his face was "radiant"; 2 Corinthians speaks of "its fleeting glory" and says the veil was "to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away". 2 Corinthians 3:18 has "unveiled faces" and "transformed into His image with intensifying glory".

rows.title: Let light shine

Gospels & Acts: You are the light of the world
let your light shine before men, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven
The letters: so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God
Let light shine out of darkness
made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ

rows.alike: Genesis 1:3 has God say "Let there be light"; 2 Corinthians 4:6 has "Let light shine out of darkness", and Matthew 5:16 "let your light shine before men".
rows.different: Genesis 1:3 and 2 Corinthians 4:6 have God say "Let there be light" and "Let light shine out of darkness"; Matthew 5:14 and 5:16 are addressed to "you": "You are the light of the world", "let your light shine before men". 2 Corinthians speaks of "the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God" and of God who "made His light shine in our hearts"; Matthew of light seen in "your good deeds".

rows.title: Like God

Genesis: you will be like God, knowing good and evil
the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil
The Prophets: I will make myself like the Most High
the house of David will be like God
Gospels & Acts: we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone
The letters: put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness
will transform our lowly bodies to be like His glorious body
We know that when Christ appears, we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is

rows.alike: Genesis 3:5 and Ephesians 4:24 both have "like God", Zechariah 12:8 says "the house of David will be like God", and Isaiah 14:14 "like the Most High"; Genesis 3:22 says "the man has become like one of Us", and 1 John 3:2 "we will be like Him".
rows.different: Genesis 3:5 gives words about eating, "in the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil", and Genesis 3:22 the LORD God's words, "the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil"; Isaiah 14:14 gives the words of one who says "I will make myself like the Most High"; Ephesians says "created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness"; 1 John and Philippians speak of what is to come, "when Christ appears" and "will transform our lowly bodies". Acts 17:29 uses "like" of "gold or silver or stone".

rows.title: A kingdom of priests

The Prophets: you will be called the priests of the LORD
Psalms & elsewhere: Now if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, you will be My treasured possession out of all the nations
unto Me you shall be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation
The letters: a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession
Revelation: Revelation 1:6
who has made us to be a kingdom, priests to His God and Father
Revelation 5:10
You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God
Revelation 20:6
they will be priests of God and of Christ

rows.alike: Exodus 19:6 has "a kingdom of priests and a holy nation", 1 Peter 2:9 "a royal priesthood, a holy nation", and Revelation "a kingdom, priests" and "a kingdom and priests"; Exodus 19:5 has "My treasured possession" and 1 Peter 2:9 "a people for God's own possession".
rows.different: Exodus 19:5-6 puts "if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant" before "you shall be a kingdom of priests"; Isaiah 61:6 says "you will be called the priests of the LORD"; 1 Peter 2:5 speaks of "offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ"; Revelation 1:6 and 5:10 say "has made us to be a kingdom, priests" and "You have made them to be a kingdom and priests", and Revelation 20:6 names them "priests of God and of Christ".

rows.title: They will reign

The Prophets: the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever-yes, forever and ever
The letters: death reigned through that one man
reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ
if we endure, we will also reign with Him
Revelation: Revelation 5:10
they will reign upon the earth
Revelation 20:4
they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years
Revelation 20:6
will reign with Him for a thousand years
Revelation 22:5
they will reign forever and ever

rows.alike: 2 Timothy 2:12 and Revelation 20:6 both have "reign with Him"; Daniel 7:18 has the kingdom possessed "forever and ever", and Revelation 22:5 "they will reign forever and ever".
rows.different: Daniel speaks of "the saints of the Most High" who "receive the kingdom"; Revelation 5:10 has "upon the earth", Revelation 20:4 and 20:6 have "for a thousand years", and Revelation 22:5 has "forever and ever"; 2 Timothy 2:12 reads "if we endure, we will also reign with Him"; Romans 5:17 sets "reign in life" beside "death reigned".

rows.title: To whom will you liken God?

The Prophets: To whom will you liken God? To what image will you compare Him?
To whom will you liken Me, or who is My equal?
To whom will you liken Me or count Me equal? To whom will you compare Me, that we should be alike?
Psalms & elsewhere: you saw no form of any kind on the day the LORD spoke to you out of the fire at Horeb
make an idol for yourselves of any form or shape
Gospels & Acts: Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man's skill and imagination

rows.alike: Isaiah asks "To what image will you compare Him?", Deuteronomy forbids "an idol for yourselves of any form or shape", and Acts says "we should not think that the Divine Being is like" "an image formed by man's skill and imagination".
rows.different: Isaiah puts it as God's question, "To whom will you liken Me"; Deuteronomy gives as its ground "you saw no form of any kind"; Acts gives as its ground "being offspring of God", after "We are His offspring".

rows.title: Exchanged their Glory for an image

The Prophets: Has a nation ever changed its gods?
But My people have exchanged their Glory for useless idols
they exchanged their Glory for a thing of disgrace
Psalms & elsewhere: They exchanged their Glory for the image of a grass-eating ox
The letters: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles

rows.alike: All four say glory was exchanged for something lesser: "exchanged their Glory for the image of a grass-eating ox", "exchanged their Glory for useless idols", "exchanged their Glory for a thing of disgrace", "exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images".
rows.different: Psalm 106 names one image, "a grass-eating ox"; Jeremiah has "useless idols" and asks "Has a nation ever changed its gods?"; Hosea has "a thing of disgrace"; Romans has "images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles" and names "the immortal God".

rows.title: An image made and worshiped

The Prophets: From the rest he makes a god, his graven image. He bows down to it and worships
Psalms & elsewhere: they made a calf and worshiped a molten image
they cast for themselves an image of a calf
Gospels & Acts: the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven
Whose image is this? And whose inscription?
Whose image and inscription are on it?
Revelation: Revelation 13:14
telling them to make an image to the beast
Revelation 13:15
so that the image could speak and cause all who refused to worship it to be killed
Revelation 14:9
If anyone worships the beast and its image and receives its mark on his forehead or on his hand
Revelation 16:2
had the mark of the beast and worshiped its image
Revelation 19:20
had the mark of the beast and worshiped its image
Revelation 20:4
those who had not worshiped the beast or its image

rows.alike: Isaiah 44:17 has "his graven image. He bows down to it and worships", Psalm 106:19 "made a calf and worshiped a molten image", Nehemiah 9:18 "cast for themselves an image of a calf", and Revelation "make an image to the beast" and "worshiped its image".
rows.different: In Psalm 106 and Nehemiah the image is of "a calf"; in Acts it is Artemis's, "which fell from heaven"; in Revelation it is "an image to the beast", made so that "the image could speak", and its worship goes with "its mark on his forehead or on his hand". The Gospels use "image" of what is on a coin: "Whose image and inscription are on it?"
